axis_reading.note: the deck's axis enters as the *flat-projected* span edge (bearing 59.769 deg), not as the anchor's committed span_bearing_deg 59.59 deg, which is the initial great-circle bearing of the same two nodes (werder_havel_aoi.bearing_deg). The two differ by 0.180 deg = 2.21 m at the far end of the deck = 0.56..0.71 px = 0.05..0.06 of a span: small, real, and committed here rather than folded away, because the m/px divided by below are flat-projected footprints and a per-span channel must not compare two different axes

crop.rule: the coordinate sits at index (200, 200): the captures were cut with r0 = round(line) - 200, c0 = round(pixel) - 200, so the request point is the rect's centre for any even side

division.rule: the documented span division of the A 10 Havelbruecke Werder: two 55 m end spans and nine 66 m inner spans, i.e. eleven openings; the residual to the deck's own 704.043 m outline is split between the two end spans, so the eleven lengths sum to the deck rather than to the rounded tag

notes: the masks are static: one crop coordinate and one fixed rect side, so the same pixel set is the mask on all 491 dates of the record. The *rect* is not quite constant - five asc_44_iw3 captures are clipped by the burst edge (394..398 of 400 lines) and are absent from the record (123 captured dates against 118 record rows) - and a clipped rect is a truncated mask: excluded by rule (inputs.clipped_captures), never stretched

the division is documented, not surveyed: the eleven openings come from the source chain above, not from a measurement in this repository. The subdivision is this file's own convention - the map's ring carries no span numbering, so ids 1..11 run from the SW end (edge 6, node 4147156906 -> 4147156911) and nothing else attaches to them

the carriageway is not in it. The record and the map carry one 35.929 m deck, not two: the OSM description names two superstructures renewed per carriageway (1995-97 and 2002-04) and the map draws their combined width. A per-carriageway channel is therefore *not* available from this geometry - it cannot be manufactured by halving a rectangle whose internal division (touching webs? shared pier line? a gap?) is not in the map

the mask is the map's rectangle. The family has measured a -81..+7 m (rms 56 m) shape error for polygon anchors (werder_havel_geometry.py): 5.7 m of it along the axis is 1.4..1.8 px = 0.08..0.10 of a span, i.e. below the span unit; across the axis it is what the matched nulls price rather than a per-span problem

--place is the live gate and the only mode that reads the external captures: it needs the harvest directory, and it exits non-zero when the placed mask is not the one the captures' own echoes show. The committed file is derived offline and does not depend on it

the placement is priced, not validated. On the rect files read on 2026-10-14 --place measures an on-mask / matched-null amplitude contrast of 0.40..0.90 in the four tracks - the deck is *not* the brightest structure in these 400 x 400 rects, the urban land west of it is - and the mirrored row sense fits two of the four better, so the gate FAILS and this file's crop point stays a quoted external fact. Everything below is therefore geometry: the census' coordinate, the documented division, the burst layer's m/px and its own orbit tag. Nothing in it is a measurement of an echo, and a per-span channel built on it inherits that limit until --place is green
